title: 2025-04-02 POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Discussed networking fixes, BGP routing flaps observed, kernel upgrade plan for the inference runtime, recent perf runs (p50/p95), and remaining security artifacts. Agreed on short action list: scheduled controlled upgrade window, extended perf run with long contexts, and finalize SOC2 docs for Nimbus security review.
next_steps: Redwood to schedule maintenance window for runtime upgrade (proposed 2025-04-04 02:00 UTC)
Customer to provide updated firewall egress rules and test endpoints by 2025-04-03
Run 10k-token throughput test and share raw logs (Redwood) by 2025-04-04
Security to review SOC2 + KMS integration notes and confirm remaining gaps (Nimbus) by 2025-04-07
action_items: Maya Chen: run 10k-token perf run with new kernel; due 2025-04-04
Jordan Patel: send updated upgrade playbook and rollback steps; due 2025-04-03
Priya Nair: open ticket with on-prem networking team for BGP flaps + share traceroute dumps; due 2025-04-03
Liam O'Connor: compile list of required KMS/HSM proofs for SOC2 review; due 2025-04-07
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Nimbus CTO), Priya (Nimbus Infra), Liam (Nimbus Security)

Summary: quick sync on Private VPC pilot. Focus on networking instability, recent perf numbers after the patch, and plan for controlled runtime/kernel upgrade.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — is this still a good time?
[00:05] Carlos: yeah all good, thanks. we had some on-call churn last night so i'm a bit scrambled but fine.
[00:12] Maya: great, i'll share my screen in a sec, got a couple slides but mostly logs and perf runs.
[00:18] Priya: quick FYI — we opened a ticket with our infra team about the BGP flaps, i put the traceroutes in the ticket.
[00:25] Jordan: perfect. can you remind the group which endpoints you're hitting from your VPC, and the egress rules? last week we saw some intermittent traffic shaping from the cloud provider.
[00:33] Priya: yes, we're hitting private-infer-01.redwood.local via NAT gateway, port 443 outbound only to 3 IPs, but our firewall was still blocking a handful of ephemeral server IPs which caused retries. i've relaxed egress for the test window.
[00:45] Maya: to add, the runtime logs showed a few connection resets and then the request retried on fallback node, which increased p95 latency. we instrumented the K-V cache lookups and saw a small bump in miss rate during the flaps.
[01:05] Carlos: is that the KV cache or K-V cache that you mean? sometimes the transcripts call it K V.
[01:10] Maya: sorry yes KV cache — key value cache. our instrumentation shows the prefix cache miss went from 2% to about 12% during the window.
[01:20] Liam: from a security POV the retries were logged but we need to confirm that the retry metadata doesn't leak any session tokens — we'll need the raw logs.
[01:30] Jordan: understood, we'll redact tokens in the logs before sharing; otherwise we can provide token-hash indices.
[01:38] Maya: moving to perf — we ran baseline 512-token runs with the quantized model on the Dedicated profile and then on the Private VPC pilot. p50 was ~85ms host-side, p95 spiked to 650ms during the network blips. post-patch (kernel optimization) p50 is ~78ms and p95 down to 320ms.
[02:00] Carlos: that's promising. the p95 is still higher than we'd like for synchronous use cases; our SLA target is 200ms p95 end-to-end.
[02:10] Maya: right, and worth noting that end-to-end includes on-prem network tail and our routing hops — some of the tail is outside Redwood's runtime (cloud nat, etc.). we proposed a couple of mitigations: more aggressive per-connection keepalive, reducing BGP session churn, and a selective traffic route via the dedicated peering.
[02:30] Priya: about peering, we have a request in with the cloud provider to allow a private peering circuit; that would avoid the NAT egress IP rotation. timeline is maybe 2 weeks. for the pilot we want small wins first.
[02:45] Jordan: agreed. the upgrade we're proposing this weekend is targeted at the inference runtime kernels — small ABI-compatible change, should reduce lock contention in KV cache paths. we plan a staged rollout: canary on 2 nodes, monitor for 30 minutes, then full sweep. rollback plan is immediate if error rate > 0.5% in canary.
[03:10] Carlos: what does immediate mean operationally? if rollback occurs do you automatically restart existing sessions?
[03:18] Maya: we will drain new connections from canary nodes and redirect to stable nodes; active sessions are allowed to finish. for long-context sessions we'll forward to fallback model to avoid state mismatch. note there might be a small quality delta for fallback.
[03:35] Liam: please document fallback quality deltas — procurement will need it for acceptance. also we need KMS integration notes: where keys are used, HSM attestation, and audit logs retention.
[03:45] Jordan: we'll send a security package. Maya, can you take point on the audit logs retention matrix?
[03:50] Maya: yep, i'll prepare the matrix and include retention options (30/90/365 days) and estimated S3 egress costs.
[04:00] Priya: on the perf tests — can you run a long-context 10k-token run? we want to see KV hot cache behavior and memory pressure across sustained load.
[04:08] Maya: yes we're scheduling a 10k-token throughput run, that's on my A-list. i expect to run it during the upgrade window to get before/after numbers.
[04:18] Carlos: are you expecting more memory issues with 10k? last time we saw GC spikes.
[04:22] Maya: the new kernel has some better slab allocation and reduced copying for KV lookups, so memory churn should be lower, but we'll monitor RSS and OOM events closely.
[04:30] Jordan: timeline check — proposed maintenance window 2025-04-04 02:00 UTC for controlled upgrade. is that ok for Nimbus?
[04:38] Priya: that's fine on our side, i'll confirm with ops and open the firewall exception for that window.
[04:42] Liam: make sure the rollback steps also include a clear audit trail — we need to capture who initiated rollback and why.
[04:50] Jordan: we'll include automated tagging in the orchestration logs for that.
[04:55] Carlos: any blockers remaining on the security front?
[05:00] Liam: we need SOC2 artifacts and KMS/HSM details; also wanting a network diagram with CIDR ranges redacted is fine.
[05:08] Jordan: i'll send the SOC2 pack and a redacted network diagram.
[05:12] Maya: quick note on routing — during the flaps we saw our load balancer switch to a fallback route that increased hops by 3 which added ~80ms. improving BGP stability or using a more static peering will remove that tail.
[05:25] Priya: do you have metrics for connection churn? that would help our network team triage.
[05:30] Maya: yes i have connection churn graphs — i'll include those in the ticket as images and raw traceroutes.
[05:38] Carlos: is there any change required to our agent config or are you just doing the runtime kernel change?
[05:44] Maya: only runtime kernel change for now; agent config remains the same, but if the peering goes live we'll suggest a keepalive tuning and slightly larger connection pools.
[05:55] Jordan: quick commercial check — you mentioned wanting an acceptance criteria for the pilot?
[06:00] Carlos: yes, baseline acceptance: p95 <= 200ms for 512-token sync calls under steady-state; no security gaps; and ability to run nightlies on 10k tokens without OOM.
[06:12] Jordan: understood. we'll aim to hit those.
[06:15] Maya: notes on benchmarking: we'll share raw logs, p50/p95 percentiles, kernel traces, and a small spreadsheet for you to compare.
[06:25] Priya: also ask — if the canary fails, what's your fallback SLA? do we pay anything?
[06:30] Jordan: for the pilot there's no extra charge; we simply rollback. for production Dedicated we have different commit terms.
[06:36] Carlos: ok thanks.
[06:40] Jordan: recap and next steps — Maya runs 10k test during upgrade window and shares logs; Jordan sends upgrade playbook + SOC2 package; Priya confirms firewall egress and peering ticket; Liam compiles KMS requests.
[06:58] Liam: one last subtlety — please include cryptographic algorithms used for transport and at-rest so our crypto reviewers can sign off.
[07:05] Jordan: will do.
[07:10] Carlos: thanks all, this was useful.
[07:12] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the maintenance calendar invite.

End of transcript.
